preamble: Vocalization of [l] all the way to the full vowel [u] happens when the lateral is itself syllabic. In Serbo-Croatian the syllabic l̩ inherited from Proto-Slavic *ьl/*ъl between consonants became u, giving vuk 'wolf' (earlier Serbian vlk) and dug 'long'. Bernese German vocalizes the syllabic [l̩] of unstressed final -el to a syllabic [u], as in Esu 'donkey' for Standard German Esel. Coda-l vocalization that produces a non-syllabic offglide (Portuguese sol [sɔw], Old French altre > autre, Bernese Halle > Hauue) is filed under l_to_w.

examples.note: Serbian spellings before about 1400 show Vlk with syllabic l; the syllabic l then became the vowel u (also in the derivative stem Vuč-).
Same development of syllabic l between consonants.
The syllabic lateral of the unstressed final syllable is replaced by the vowel [u]; Bernese l-vocalization also turns coda /l/ into a glide elsewhere.
